title: Cost of the deterministic small-bias Fourier estimator
statement: Let the input consist of a positive dimension $n$, positive integers $a$ and $b$ with $2a \le b$, and an integer Fourier bound $B \ge 1$. Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, and let $U$ be a finite set of coordinates in that cube. Running the deterministic query program with oracle $f$ returns the average of $f(x)\prod_{i\in U}x_i$ over the program's prescribed sample, together with its cost: zero random examples and membership queries, and local work equal to the deterministic construction work plus the Fourier estimator work.
hypotheses_covered: positive dimension of the bias input
twice the bias numerator is at most the bias denominator
real-valued oracle on the sign cube of the generator dimension
